Island effect showers thunderstorms are the main forecast concern 
for Guam over the next couple of days, with light and variable winds 
expected for at least the first half of the week. Otherwise, 
isolated light showers will be the rule through Monday as the 
overall dry pattern continues. For the CNMI, expect increasing 
convection Monday night as a weak disturbance passes by to the east 
of the islands, coming close enough to the CNMI to bring low-end 
scattered showers and possible thunderstorms. This convection will 
spread into Guam Tuesday night. This round of showers will be 
relatively short- lived, with a dry pattern returning to the region 
Wednesday morning. The dry pattern will then continue through next 
weekend.

Marine/Surf...
Not much of a change in the marine and surf forecast. Combined seas
of 3 to 5 feet will begin to slowly build around midweek as the
trade-wind swell builds over the area. Surf will slowly increase as
well, reaching up to 5 feet along north facing reefs Monday night,
resulting in a moderate risk of rip currents. The rip current risk
will remain moderate along east facing reefs for the next several 
days.

Tropical Systems...
A weak disturbance found along the monsoon trough, Invest 90W, is 
centered along an area of sharp troughing, just west of a 
circulation center found north of Pohnpei, near 12N156E. 90W is  
rated low, meaning development is unlikely over the next 24 hours. 
Invest 90W will generally drift NW over the next couple of days and 
looks to consolidate within the weak circulation center a little 
farther east than the current centroid location. 90W is expected to 
slowly strengthen over the coming days as it moves in the general 
direction of Maug in the northern CNMI. 

For more information on Invest 90W, see bulletins issued by the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
A trough has moved out of Majuro but environmental conditions 
remain unstable so scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms 
remain possible tonight and continuing through the entire forecast
period as new troughs move into the area. Gentle winds tonight 
will become lighter throughout the week, becoming light and 
variable by Wednesday. Seas of 4 to 5 feet are expected to persist
through the whole forecast period.

A ridge has formed over Kosrae and is expected to keep the island
dry through Wednesday with only isolated showers expected. By 
Thursday, the monsoon trough may push back into the region and 
bring scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms. Seas will 
remain at 5 feet for most of the forecast period. 

As 90W pushes to the north-northwest, only low end scattered 
showers and isolated thunderstorms remain tonight for Pohnpei, 
becoming isolated showers by tomorrow. However, the monsoon is 
expected to redevelop over the island with more scattered showers 
and isolated thunderstorms anticipated Monday night and Tuesday 
before another brief dry spell. A new weak trough may develop near
Pohnpei Thursday to bring more precipitation but confidence 
remains low. Seas of 5 to 6 feet tonight will continue for at 
least the next few days.

Western Micronesia...
A Small Craft and High Surf Advisory has been issued for Chuuk
through at least Tuesday.

The main feature affecting the region is the monsoon flow with a few
embedded circulations, one of which is Invest 90W.

There are two circulations embedded within the monsoon flow, the 
first, is located near 12N134E, to the northwest of Yap Proper and
north of Palau, and the second is Invest 90W mentioned above in the 
Tropical Systems Section.

The first circulation is producing scattered showers along the
southern flank over Palau. This feature is expected to keep 
scattered to numerous showers over Palau through the middle of next 
week. This will provide some much needed rain to the region.

Invest 90W is located near 12N156E (north of Pohnpei) and is pulling
a lot of moisture from south of the Equator. This is producing 
numerous showers along a convergence axis from EQ142E to 12N156E, 
passing over Chuuk lagoon. Satellite imagery shows numerous showers 
along this axis, however, model guidance is showing widespread 
showers. Showers are expected to begin tapering down as early as 
Tuesday night. Dry and near breezy conditions are anticipated to 
return once this feature moves westward.

Altimetry shows combined seas of 3 to 5 feet for much of Yap State.
Combined seas near Chuuk is estimated to be near 8 feet. The primary
swell for Palau and Yap is from the west, while the primary swell at
Chuuk is from the south generated by a low-pressure system south of 
the equator. Surf along south facing reefs has exceeded the 9 foot

Tuesday. As features move westward, west facing reefs may also exceed
